findings.summary: Reader proxy request-header filtering duplicates the red asset proxy policy.
findings.consequence: Future changes to the content proxy trust boundary can drift between /txt, /bilder, /export/faksimil, and /red; one route could start forwarding a newly sensitive or newly required header while the other keeps different behavior.
findings.evidence: readerRequestHeaders builds an allowlisted Headers object from accept/cache validators/range headers while honoring hop-by-hop names from Connection. The direct caller context includes server/routes/red/[...path].ts contentRequestHeaders with the same header list and Connection filtering behavior, while backend-proxy.ts has another related proxy header policy.
findings.recommendation: Extract a small shared content-proxy request-header helper that takes the allowed header names, applies connectionHeaderNames once, and use it from both reader-source-proxy.ts and server/routes/red/[...path].ts.

Inspected test/integration/reader-runtime-proxy.spec.ts for observable header forwarding coverage.

findings.summary: Disconnect abort handling is duplicated across proxy modules.
findings.consequence: A future fix to request-abort or response-close cleanup may need to be applied in multiple places; missing one copy can leave an upstream fetch running after the client disconnects or remove listeners inconsistently.
findings.evidence: abortOnDisconnect registers the same req aborted and res close listeners used by server/utils/backend-proxy.ts and server/routes/red/[...path].ts, including the writableEnded guard and cleanup closure.
findings.recommendation: Move the common abort-on-disconnect helper to a shared server proxy utility and keep only proxy-specific behavior in each route/module.
